text:
maria: Quick bench summary: 24h runs across us-west / eu-west comparing L4, T4, A10G for embeddings (batching-heavy) and small-chat (autoregressive). Headline numbers and notes below.

dan: Can you drop a compact table (p50/p95, throughput, cost/1M) so I can paste into the slides?

maria: Sure — copied from the aggregated run (all runs used same model binary + quant profiles where noted). seq_len for small-chat = 128, embedding tokens ~64, batching as indicated. Numbers are single-GPU sustained averages with 20% headroom buffer applied.

maria: ```
Workload      | GPU   | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | throughput  | est cost / 1M units
--------------|-------|----------|----------|-------------|--------------------
Embeddings    | L4    | 0.10 ms  | 0.25 ms  | 9.8k qps    | $0.42 / 1M embeds
              | A10G  | 0.13 ms  | 0.35 ms  | 7.1k qps    | $0.55 / 1M embeds
              | T4    | 0.28 ms  | 0.7 ms   | 3.3k qps    | $1.05 / 1M embeds
Small-chat    | L4    | 11 ms/t | 28 ms/t  | 85 tok/s    | $0.17 / 1M tokens
              | A10G  | 16 ms/t | 42 ms/t  | 60 tok/s    | $0.22 / 1M tokens
              | T4    | 30 ms/t | 82 ms/t  | 32 tok/s    | $0.38 / 1M tokens
```

maria: Notes: 
- Embedding numbers are query/sec at batch size 64 with async batching window 10ms.
- Small-chat measured as tokens/sec (autoregressive, batch=1 simulated concurrency 64).
- Cost numbers use list prices we used in last quarter: L4 cheaper per-hour than A10G in our cloud pricing, T4 cheaper but much lower throughput so cost/perf is worse.

eva: Nice. How much did quantization help? We tried q4_0 and int8 in these runs right?

maria: Right. Summary: q4_0 (4-bit) improved throughput by ~1.7x on T4 and ~1.4x on A10G for embeddings; on L4 the win was smaller (~1.25x) because the L4 kernels we used already leverage mixed-int8 pathways. For small-chat int8/q4 gave ~1.5x token/sec on T4, ~1.2x on A10G, ~1.1x on L4. Quality regressions were negligible on our eval set (embedding cosine sigma < 0.5%, small-chat BLEU-like auto-metric delta < 0.8) but we flagged a few low-prob hallucination cases for manual review.

chris: Which kernel stacks were you running? flash-attn vs fused-triton vs cuBLAS?

maria: We tested 3 stacks: flash-attn-2 fused kernels (default on L4), triton-fused attention (experiment), and fallback path using cuBLAS matmul + custom KV. Quick take: 
- L4: flash-attn fused wins at seq_len <=512 across both workloads.
- A10G: triton-fused slightly faster for latency-critical small-chat at seq<=256; for larger batch embeddings flash-attn parity.
- T4: older kernels, often limited by memory-bandwidth — flash-attn helps but still behind.

maria: Also saw KV cache eviction patterns matter: when we pinned kv-pages and used prefetching on L4, effective p95 improved by ~12% for small-chat multi-turn. On T4 we saw tail spikes when cache fragmented (we suspect driver fragmentation).

benchbot: automated: run_2161234567_meta: runs=24, regions=2, quant_profiles=[fp16,q4_0,int8], kernel_variants=[flash, triton, cuBLAS], dataset=embed-synth-1k + chat-eval-2k.

dan: For capacity planning — if a customer needs 100k embed qps sustained (99th), how many GPUs?

maria: Quick calc: using our sustained qps per GPU above (with 20% headroom):
- L4: ~9.8k -> need 12 L4s (11.2 -> round up to 12)
- A10G: ~7.1k -> need 15 A10G
- T4: ~3.3k -> need 31 T4
These already include buffer for autoscaling headroom and networking overhead.

eva: And for a small-chat product with 50 concurrent users each generating 40 tok/s peak? (2000 tok/s aggregate)

maria: 2000 tok/s / per-GPU tok/s =>
- L4: 2000/85 ~ 24 GPUs (we recommend 30 with canary + 20% slack)
- A10G: 2000/60 ~ 34 GPUs (recommend 40)
- T4: 2000/32 ~ 63 GPUs (recommend 75)

chris: Any region delta? eu-west added net +3–6ms p50 depending on instance family?

maria: Yes — cross-region routing (us-west client -> eu-west GPU) adds ~40–80ms; comparing same-region us-west vs eu-west we saw eu-west~+3ms p50 and +5–8ms p95 (likely NIC placement / instance type differences). So for latency-SLO customers, colocate.

chris: Were these runs with our smart-batching (continuous batching) on? That changes tail behavior.

maria: Yes, continuous batching enabled with adaptive windows. Turning it off drops throughput ~20% on embeddings but reduces single-request jitter for very low QPS use cases. We documented the knob in the run notes.
